issues.body: `char_sets_complete_for` sorts each key but does not reject or deduplicate repeated predicates within a `CharSet`. Thus `{p}` and `{p,p}` compare as distinct keys although they denote the same exact predicate set, and `char_set_has` counts each entry once. Supplying `{p}` plus `{p,p}`, and `{q}` plus `{q,q}`, with balanced `distinct_subjects` totals and no served `{p,q}` cohort can make both completeness checks pass. Rule C2 may then report the same-source pairing dead and prune a combination that can actually contribute. The new negative test exercises duplicate identical keys only, so it does not catch this case.
issues.fix_hint: Canonicalize every characteristic-set key as a mathematical set before the repeated-key check, or fail closed when any key contains a duplicate predicate. Add the prior-round non-vacuous negative test using `{p}`, `{p,p}`, `{q}`, and `{q,q}` with balanced totals and no served co-occurrence key; assert that no dead pairing or prune is emitted.
issues.title: Duplicate predicates within a characteristic-set key still bypass the partition guard

verdict.summary: The round-three major recall-safety finding remains. The new repeated-key guard rejects two characteristic-set entries only when their sorted predicate vectors are exactly equal, but it neither rejects nor canonicalizes duplicate predicates within one key. Consequently `{p}` and `{p,p}` remain distinct keys even though characteristic sets represent mathematical predicate sets. Balanced malformed singleton/multiset entries can still satisfy both per-predicate accounting equalities while omitting the real co-occurrence cohort, causing Rule C2 to emit a dead pairing and potentially suppress a live combination. The added `duplicate_char_sets_decline_the_prune` test covers repeated identical entries, not this prior-round counterexample. Progress is therefore stagnant.
